subject: How to prevent collision of axis tick label in facet_grid?

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: How to prevent collision of axis tick label in facet_grid?
parts:
How can one prevent the collision of axis tick label on adjacent facets? (without complicated code to manipulate limits/breaks)

The code below generates a 2x2 grid in which the last tick mark label for the facets on left collides with the first such label for the facets on the right.

  data = data.frame(expand.grid(n=c(50, 100), type=c("A","B"), hor=c(1:24)), ver=rnorm(96))
  library(ggplot2)
  ggplot(data, aes(x=hor, y=ver)) + geom_point() + 
    facet_grid("type ~ n", labeller = label_both) + 
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = rel(1.5)))

In this case, "25" and "0" are plotted over each other.  I figure the easiest way would be to hide the first tick mark label, the "0", but I don't know to specify that.

Any suggestions would be appreciated.  Thanks

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: How to prevent collision of axis tick label in facet_grid?
parts:
Hi:

Here are three options; there are undoubtedly others.

dat <- data.frame(expand.grid(n=c(50, 100), type=c("A","B"),
hor=c(1:24)), ver=rnorm(96))

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=hor, y=ver)) + geom_point() +

facet_grid("type ~ n", labeller = label_both) +
theme(axis.text = element_text(size = rel(1.5)))

# Redefine the breaks
p + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(5, 20, by = 5))

# Artificially expand the limits of the x-range
p + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-2.5, 27.5),
breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5))
# Increase the spacing between panels
p + theme(panel.margin = grid::unit(0.2, "in"))

I prefer the second one, but YMMV.

Dennis

parts:
Dennis ... thank you for the suggestions.

The first two are not quite usable as I won't know the range of the x-axis (other than all values will be greater than 0), thus I can't change the breaks or expand the axis based on hard-coded. values.

The third suggestion (increasing the facet margin is one I can use.  Too bad it uses up some screen real estate unproductively.

Ideally, I was hoping to somehow access the breaks labels computed by default ... then somehow re-specifying them ... perhaps using "" as the first label.

Thanks again
